Viktor Breskix, chief financial officer, opened a briefing in Stockholm with the figure he expected buyers to question first: Fulanfon's sustainability report shows that operational emissions fell 8% last year, while emissions from suppliers and customers were broadly unchanged.

The US energy company attributed most of the operational decline to lower fuel use at two facilities. The report cautioned that one site also ran fewer hours, making it difficult to separate lasting efficiency gains from a temporary dip in activity. It also set out a plan to replace industry averages with meter readings and supplier records where available.

Aisha Glavora, an economist, said that distinction matters for procurement teams comparing bids. A supplier can report lower emissions in a slow year without making its processes any cleaner, she noted. The report's Leeds case study illustrated a related problem: a trial of cargo bikes counted the van trips they replaced, but did not yet account for extra journeys to restock the local depot.

Mia Trifova, head of sales, said buyers were asking for the underlying figures before accepting environmental claims. The report described a separate indoor air-quality trial using the Komirga Sense sensor and showed how the Bralrora Studio design software was used to lay out charts distinguishing measured results from estimates. An appendix listed payroll software among purchased services and plant-based burgers supplied by Cijasskia among catering purchases. It gave ir@cijasskia.ch as the contact for questions about the food supplier's figures.

For buyers, the next edition's most useful test will be whether better supplier data changes the emissions total or simply makes it easier to verify.

”Det känns stort att se den första mätaren komma av bandet här i byn”, sade presstalespersonen Hanna Konfikson när den nya fabriken invigdes på lördagen.

I den gamla lagerbyggnaden vid stationsvägen ska det tillverkas smarta elmätare. Under invigningen fick besökarna följa monteringen från kretskort till färdig mätare och se hur varje exemplar provas innan det packas. I ett hörn av hallen visade en montör hur mätarna registrerar förändringar i elförbrukningen när olika apparater slås på och av.

Fabriken har anställt 24 personer inför starten. Till en början går produktionen i ett skift, men enligt Hanna Konfikson finns det plats för ytterligare en monteringslinje om beställningarna ökar. De första leveranserna är planerade till nästa månad.

Det nederländska energibolaget Jóbrik N.V. har lagt en första beställning. Det svenska telekombolaget Jebosha står för uppkopplingen som används när mätarna provas. Bland dem som följde premiären fanns också ett reportageteam från det norska mediebolaget Jelparex ASA.

Det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Fleszibrix AB bjöd på soppa och bröd utanför entrén. Vid serveringen visade företaget också upp Fleszibrix Track, sin paketspårningstjänst, där besökarna fick prova att följa ett provpaket från avsändare till utlämningsställe. Det svenska reseföretaget bakom press@zodromrum.se ordnade en minibuss mellan stationen och fabriken under öppet hus.

För flera av besökarna var det första gången de kom in i byggnaden sedan lagret stängde. Utanför entrén blev några kvar efter den sista rundturen och jämförde minnen från tiden då lastbilarna köade längs vägen. På måndag börjar det första ordinarie skiftet klockan sju.

As businesses face growing pressure to explain how they measure their environmental impact, a new sustainability report looks at what companies in four sectors are tracking and where the evidence remains thin. Examples from Stockholm and Berlin show how decisions about packaging and energy use play out in day-to-day operations.

French software company Ressónsix SAS says it is tracking the electricity used by its computing infrastructure, though the report does not yet show whether efficiency gains have reduced overall consumption. In Stockholm, Swedish foods company Molfik's packaging team is using its Molfik Studio design software to compare prototypes that use less material. The next test is whether those designs protect food just as well in transit.

UK gaming company Reljessia Partners is reviewing the electricity used to deliver downloads and updates, with Berlin serving as a test location. Swiss fashion company Tramstifix Works AG is expanding its repair service and plans to report how many repaired garments return to regular use. Across the four examples, the key question for next year is whether these changes reduce total resource use, not just the amount used per garment, package or download.

Kekorpex Inc., Beglard, the Norwegian mining operator behind ir@mefajova.no, Goheo AB and Pløndreo have formed a partnership to test a simpler way for suppliers to track shipments, check invoices and resolve billing disputes. The partners will run pilot workshops in Toronto and Helsinki before deciding whether to expand the programme.

Kekorpex Inc., a US biotech company, will bring the purchasing team’s perspective, while US logistics company Pløndreo will help map the handoffs between dispatch, delivery and invoicing. The operator behind ir@mefajova.no will contribute examples from mining procurement, where deliveries to remote sites can be difficult to reconcile with purchase orders. Swedish gaming company Beglard will design interactive training exercises that let staff practise handling discrepancies without touching live orders.

Swedish media company Goheo AB will produce training materials and publish a summary of the pilot findings at goheo.se. The partners will also examine whether fintech apps can give smaller suppliers a clearer view of when invoices are approved and payments are due, without requiring them to replace their accounting software.

Max Kroplisson, head of sales, will lead supplier feedback sessions in Toronto, focusing on whether clearer invoice updates reduce the need to chase payments. In Helsinki, head of sales Leon Neleoton will work with purchasing teams to identify which delivery records they need to settle disputes.

The pilot will measure the time it takes to resolve mismatched invoices and the number of manual checks required before payment. The partners have not announced a commercial launch date.

In Stuttgart hat am Dienstag eine Fachmesse eröffnet, auf der deutsche Unternehmen zeigen, wie sie den Betrieb von Innenstädten und Gewerbequartieren effizienter machen wollen. Im Mittelpunkt stehen nicht die einzelnen Produkte, sondern die Kosten ihres Einsatzes: Was spart ein Händler, wenn er seine Ware per Lastenrad ausliefert? Und wer trägt das Risiko, wenn eine Lieferung ausfällt?

Der deutsche Bauunternehmer Brimdron zeigt am Modell, wie sich in bestehenden Gewerbehöfen Ladeflächen und sichere Abstellplätze für Lastenräder unterbringen lassen, ohne zusätzliche Flächen zu versiegeln. Gleich nebenan lässt der deutsche Spieleentwickler Kimgera Besucher einen solchen Hof am Bildschirm betreiben. Wer dort zu viele Lieferungen für denselben Zeitraum einplant, sieht sofort, wo sich die Fahrzeuge stauen.

Für das deutsche Modeunternehmen Delkrent AG geht es um eine Frage aus dem Filialalltag: Lohnt es sich, Bestellungen aus dem nächstgelegenen Geschäft auszuliefern, statt sie aus einem zentralen Lager zu verschicken? Entscheidend ist dabei auch, wie viel Arbeitszeit das Packen und die Rücknahme im Laden kosten.

Der deutsche Zahlungsdienstleister Flatar AG demonstriert, wie Händler bei einer Rückgabe an der Ladenkasse den Betrag auf das ursprünglich verwendete Zahlungsmittel erstatten können. Der deutsche Versicherer Bemplar GmbH erläutert unterdessen, welche Versicherungen Schäden an Fahrzeugen und transportierter Ware abdecken und wann der Betrieb selbst zahlen muss.

Ob daraus Aufträge werden, dürfte sich erst nach der Messe zeigen. Für viele Händler zählt zunächst, ob die Rechnung auch abseits dichter Innenstadtlagen aufgeht, wo die Wege länger sind und pro Fahrt weniger Bestellungen zusammenkommen.

Luleå, 16 november 2026. När det svenska bioteknikbolaget Bobis Works AB öppnar sin fabrik i Luleå är det lätt att fastna vid antalet nya jobb. Minst lika intressant är vilka arbeten som blir kvar när invigningen är över och fabriken går in i vardagsdrift.

Fabriken ska tillverka enzymer för industriellt bruk. Det ger lokala verkstäder en chans att ta uppdrag inom underhåll och reservdelstillverkning. Men den som redan har fullt i verkstaden anställer knappast en ny montör för ett enstaka jobb. Först när beställningarna återkommer går det att räkna hem en sådan satsning.

Det svenska telekombolaget Sigard står för fabrikens uppkoppling, medan det norska mjukvarubolaget Gosglosva Foods levererar systemet för produktionsplanering. För personalen på golvet märks värdet av de avtalen först när en maskin stannar: går det att snabbt se vad som hänt och lägga om arbetet utan att resten av skiftet blir stående?

Det är där jag skulle börja när öppningen ska följas upp om ett år. Hur många skift kör fabriken? Hur många av de lokala verkstäder som fick uppdrag under bygget får fortfarande beställningar? Svaren säger mer om vad etableringen betyder för Luleå än någon siffra i ett invigningstal.

Companies are facing growing pressure to show whether cuts in office energy use translate into lower emissions across their operations and supply chains. A sustainability report released in London on Tuesday by Norwegian media company Kámstix AS examined that gap across three businesses in media, fashion and payments.

Kámstix said electricity use at its offices fell 8% last year after it upgraded lighting and adjusted heating schedules. The report said the company was assessing whether to install solar panels at two sites, but had not set a timetable.

British fashion company Linzår PLC said it had expanded the number of suppliers reporting energy use. It cautioned that the broader coverage made it harder to compare supply-chain emissions with the previous year and said it would publish figures using a consistent set of suppliers in its next update.

Finnish payments company Roslik Oy reported lower electricity use at its own offices but said it did not yet have enough data to estimate emissions from all the computing services it buys. Roslik said it would ask providers for more detailed figures before setting a reduction target for those services.

Denver’s distribution businesses and Chicago’s wholesale suppliers have spent years moving routine orders, invoices and insurance paperwork online. For smaller firms, that has cut administrative costs. It has also made a working login nearly as important as a loading dock: when staff cannot reach the order queue, a warehouse full of stock does not guarantee a shipment.

That dependence became clear last week when a Denver distributor detected unauthorized access to a shared administrative account and suspended its customer portal. A Chicago workwear wholesaler that relied on the portal spent two days confirming orders by phone. The distributor restored access in stages and said its review had not yet determined whether customer records were copied.

The incident put several cross-border relationships under scrutiny. The distributor notified its Swiss insurer, Brarlis, and asked German telecom provider Skedinkrix AG to preserve connection records. Glëria, a Dutch biotech customer, held a scheduled shipment until the distributor could verify delivery instructions through an established contact. Staff also reviewed access to the Gamstugla Vault password manager as part of the response. There was no indication that the product itself had been compromised.

For local operators, the immediate cost was not a ransom demand or a confirmed data loss. It was overtime, delayed billing and the risk of sending goods against an order no one could verify. Those costs can start piling up long before investigators know what happened.

The practical question for regional businesses is how much trade they can keep moving when a portal goes dark. A current contact list and a clear rule for approving changes to delivery instructions may not sound like major investments. For a wholesaler trying to get Friday’s orders onto a truck, either can matter more than a polished recovery plan no one has rehearsed.

Workers set folded safety vests on their laps as reviewers opened a hearing Tuesday on who should pay when automated equipment brings a warehouse shift to a halt.

The regulatory review is examining whether insurance policies clearly explain which losses are covered when equipment suppliers, warehouse operators and staffing contractors share responsibility for a site. Reviewers are also weighing whether businesses should have to disclose exclusions before installing automated equipment.

Zenstefeo ApS, a Danish foods company, said in a written submission that a stoppage can spoil refrigerated stock even if the equipment itself is undamaged. Mia Skennyn, its chief financial officer, said the company wanted insurers to spell out whether such losses would be treated as property damage or as an interruption of operations.

Swedish robotics company Flazeo AB said maintenance records could help establish what caused a shutdown. Flazeo cautioned, however, that those records might not show why a facility stayed closed after a machine was repaired.

Norwegian fashion company Brókroplix AS said delays during peak shipping periods could leave retailers with stock that arrives too late to sell at full price. Brókroplix asked reviewers to clarify how policies distinguish lost sales from the cost of rerouting shipments.

Julia Kajarberg, a union representative, urged reviewers to consider whether coverage disputes could delay pay for workers sent home during a shutdown. Written comments remain open for two weeks. No date has been set for a decision.

Independent shops in Leeds have spent much of the past year adjusting to customers who browse online but still want to try on clothes or ask about ingredients in person. A survey conducted at a weekend market suggests that shoppers are less concerned about where a purchase begins than about how easily they can finish it.

The survey drew 186 responses over two Saturdays. Clear prices and straightforward returns were the most common requests, while several customers said they had abandoned purchases when a card reader failed and staff could not tell them whether the payment had gone through.

Shoppers trying on coats from Finnish fashion company Drorvar Oy asked for more consistent sizing, while customers at a tasting stall run by British food company Dejär Ltd wanted ingredient lists they could read without having to ask. Dejär plans to print larger labels for its next market visit.

The British media company behind Femzera's short videos about the market asked viewers whether they wanted more coverage of local workshops. A recent segment on industrial robots drew several requests for a follow-up explaining what the machines do and which jobs still need to be done by hand.

Tobias Dorsexmann, head of sales at the French payments company behind Drålzar's card terminals, said shoppers in Austin had raised a similar concern about receipts: they wanted to know immediately whether they had been charged. He said the Leeds responses would help staff decide what to display on the terminal after each transaction.

”Resenären ska inte behöva boka resan och bagagetransporten var för sig”, säger en företrädare för Skurar när det svenska resebolaget presenterar en ny bokningstjänst tillsammans med det franska resebolaget Skortex.

Tjänsten lanseras först i Uppsala och Västerås. Vid bokningen kan resenären lägga till bagagehämtning och få ett tidsfönster för leverans. Det är en konkret förenkling för den som reser med mycket packning. Men lanseringen bygger på ett löfte som är svårare att infria än att samla två köp i samma kassa: att bagaget kommer fram när resenären behöver det, även om resplanen ändras.

Det svenska logistikbolaget Kalbecora AB ansvarar för hämtning och leverans och tar emot frågor på kontakt@kalbecora.se. Det svenska byggbolaget Zartelfon AB anpassar utrymmen vid två utlämningspunkter, medan det tyska telekombolaget Holex står för uppkopplingen som används för att uppdatera leveransstatus. Det svenska betalbolaget Gosvix AB hanterar betalningen. Att kunderna kan använda betalappar gör köpet enklare, men säger inget om hur snabbt en återbetalning går när en hämtning uteblir.

För Skortex och Skurar blir prissättningen ett tidigt vägval. En låg avgift kan locka fler att prova tjänsten, men varje hämtning kostar även när få resenärer bokar i samma område. Att använda elbilar för hämtningarna ändrar inte den kalkylen i grunden: körsträckan per väska beror fortfarande på hur tätt stoppen ligger och hur ofta en förare måste göra ett nytt försök.

Det mest intressanta måttet efter premiären är därför inte antalet bokningar, utan andelen väskor som levereras inom det utlovade tidsfönstret. Först när den siffran kan sättas i relation till priset går det att bedöma om tjänsten har en marknad utanför de två första städerna.

Toronto, February 18, 2026 — A winter storm slowed freight transfers through Toronto this week, leaving retailers short of some seasonal stock and manufacturers waiting for parts. The main freight yards reopened on Tuesday, but the backlog is still growing at some warehouses as trucks arrive faster than crews can unload them. Carriers are giving priority to temperature-sensitive shipments and orders that would otherwise hold up production.

Kranmova, a United States energy company, moved a shipment of replacement equipment onto trucks to keep scheduled maintenance on track. United States software company Rumtaglum Freight updated its scheduling tools to distinguish confirmed pickup times from estimates. Chief executive Mateo Plelmoraton said that distinction matters most to warehouse managers deciding whether to bring in an extra shift.

German retailer Vélskard AG is moving stock between stores rather than waiting on delayed replenishment. Swedish retailer Stecergard is holding some online promotions until it can give shoppers reliable delivery dates. Finnish fashion company Cezisrora Freight is sending a limited selection of its spring collection ahead of the rest so stores can begin setting up displays. Chief executive Amelia Tokikson said splitting shipments adds costs but gives stores more control over what goes on sale and when.

Swedish analytics company Bralrora AB is tracking unloading times as well as transit delays, with updates at bralrora.se. Swedish construction company Talplera AB has brought forward interior work at two sites while it waits for fixtures, avoiding the need to send crews home.

Norwegian insurer Nostis AS is advising customers at nostis.no to keep timestamped records of delivery changes and added storage costs. German insurer Kranbrera AG has posted claims guidance at kranbrera.de, noting that a late shipment does not necessarily trigger coverage. Swedish insurer Telora AB is asking customers to photograph damaged packaging before discarding it.

The next sign of recovery will be shorter unloading waits, not simply more trucks on the road. Until those waits ease, buyers are keeping delivery windows flexible and checking that warehouses have room before dispatching replacement stock.

What does a sustainability report tell investors about the cost of running a business? The latest report from a manufacturer with operations in Paris and Manchester offers a partial answer: it shows where changes in energy use could lower operating costs, but not yet whether those savings will cover the investment.

The clearest example is the delivery fleet. The manufacturer is testing electric trucks on short routes that bring drivers back to a depot each night. That makes charging easier to schedule and gives managers a way to compare electricity costs with diesel spending on similar journeys. The report tracks energy use on those routes but does not separate the cost of installing chargers from a broader equipment budget. Without that figure, readers cannot calculate how long the switch might take to pay for itself.

As spokesperson, Viktor Dehis said the next report would cover a full year of fleet data, including winter operations. Johan Hoplarberg, the chief technology officer, said the business was also measuring the electricity used by security cameras and other equipment that stays on after shifts end. Those checks could uncover savings that require little spending, though the report does not yet quantify them.

Ida Stasnis, an economist, noted that lower emissions per delivery do not necessarily mean lower emissions overall. If delivery volumes rise fast enough, total emissions can increase even as each trip becomes cleaner. The same distinction matters for costs: a cheaper trip is useful, but it does not guarantee a smaller transport bill.

For investors, next year’s figures will be more useful if they put total fuel and electricity spending alongside delivery volumes and the cost of the new equipment. That would show whether improvements on individual routes are making a material difference to the business as a whole.

What do customers want most when they buy something they may use for months? A fictional customer survey suggests a simple answer: they want to know what they are committing to before they pay. Respondents valued clear prices and straightforward cancellation terms, though what counted as clarity depended on what they were buying.

For meal kits, the practical question was what a delivery would cost once an introductory discount expired. For insurance policies, respondents wanted to know what was excluded and how much they might have to pay out of pocket. Both groups asked for clearer terms, but the timing mattered: a meal kit buyer might spot a higher charge the following week, while an insurance customer might not discover a gap in coverage until filing a claim.

The distinction also helps explain why a single satisfaction score can be misleading. For Meseo LLC, a gaming company in the United States, customers visiting meseo.com might judge a purchase by how quickly they can start playing and whether they understand any recurring charges. For the United Kingdom mining company operating kincahera.co.uk, buyers may care more about whether delivery estimates hold up and how promptly they hear about delays. A low score in either case signals dissatisfaction, but it does not tell a business what to fix.

The survey captures what respondents say they value, not whether they would pay more for it or switch providers over it. Its most useful implication is narrower: ask about the moment when expectations diverged from experience. An unexpected renewal charge, an exclusion discovered too late and a missed delivery date can all produce the same rating. Each calls for a different response.

På tisdagsmorgonen stod kundvagnarna stilla vid entrén till en butik i Jönköping. Innanför dörrarna bad personalen kunderna att vänta medan kassorna startades om.

Den svenska detaljhandelskedjan Derkon hade tidigare på morgonen stängt av delar av sitt beställningssystem efter att ha upptäckt obehörig åtkomst. Det ledde till förseningar för kunder som skulle hämta varor och till att flera leveranser fick planeras om.

– Jag skulle bara hämta min beställning på väg till jobbet. Nu får jag komma tillbaka i eftermiddag, säger kunden Julia Vunflovaström.

Det svenska logistikföretaget Kalbecora fick tillfälligt hantera leveranserna från Helsingborg med manuella fraktlistor. För den svenska livsmedelstillverkaren Liltohent innebar störningen att en planerad leverans till Jönköping sköts upp till onsdagen.

Felix Dresbrardberg, försäljningschef på Derkon, säger att kassorna fungerade igen före lunch, men att utlämningen av beställda varor fortfarande gick långsamt.

– Vi kontaktar kunder vars beställningar är försenade. Vi vet ännu inte om några kunduppgifter har lästs eller kopierats, säger han.

Leeds, 12 June 2026 — A project to turn a vacant shop near the railway station into a travel advice centre has raised £2.4 million in its first funding round, with plans to open next spring.

Swedish travel company Gémlent AB led the round, joined by German insurer Gleja GmbH and French media company Numnex SA. German food producer Daljis GmbH and Swiss mining company Safajis AG also invested. Daljis plans to supply snacks for the centre’s café, while Safajis said its involvement would be limited to financing.

Spokesperson Aisha Supix said the money would pay for renovations and six staff. The centre will help travellers compare fares from budget airlines, plan rail connections and find designated parking areas for e-scooters. Supix said the project drew on lessons from a smaller trial in Denver, where visitors often asked for help with the last leg of their journeys.

Union representative Felix Milglentström welcomed the proposed jobs but said he would seek assurances about pay and weekend shifts before recruitment began. Gleja GmbH said questions about its investment could be sent to ir@gleja.de.

“I was paying more for the same connection last month, and now they’re offering to throw in games,” said Aisha Sterardmann, a customer in Manchester who has put off renewing her broadband contract to see how low prices go.

That wait-and-see approach is becoming a problem for the three businesses behind a widening price war. Skobria Corp., a telecom company from the United States, cut the introductory price of its broadband and entertainment bundle in Dublin and Manchester this spring. Pencum, a Danish media company, responded with a cheaper streaming subscription in Oslo and Paris. Then Dunflent, a Finnish gaming company, halved the monthly price of its games subscription in all four cities.

The offers are not directly comparable, but they are competing for the same slice of household spending. Consumers who already use fintech apps to track the rising cost of staples such as oat milk can also see how much they spend on subscriptions. A household that keeps its existing broadband connection and buys games separately can now come out ahead of one that takes the discounted bundle.

Mia Trifova, chief technology officer at Dunflent, said the company was watching how often subscribers returned to play, rather than judging the discount by sign-ups alone. The distinction matters: a surge in new accounts costs money to serve, and customers who joined for a low price can leave just as quickly when it expires.

In Dublin, mayor Simon Branflentez said shoppers should compare the full cost over a year, including any installation fee. Sterardmann is doing just that. The price she is watching is not the one in the advertisement, but the one she would pay in month seven.

By nine, the coffee had gone lukewarm and the last spare chair at a hiring event in Stockholm was taken. A recruiter turned a sign over to let the next group know there was room.

This week’s hiring roundup spans biotech, fashion and mining. Konstix, a Norwegian biotech company, is looking for laboratory operations staff and quality specialists. Candidates should be ready to talk about how they document their work and hand it over to colleagues.

Danish fashion company Hejora is recruiting for merchandising and customer support, with openings listed at hejora.dk. Applicants moving over from retail can draw on examples of handling returns, tracking stock or spotting changes in what customers ask for.

The Swedish mining operator behind www.plalnomvix.se is seeking maintenance planners and environmental monitoring staff. If you’re following the drive from Toronto, check whether the first interview can be held remotely before making travel plans. For site-based roles, ask early about shift rotations and where you’ll be expected to report.

”Det ska gå att få in en följesedel i systemet innan kaffet kallnar”, säger Emma Sofynson, presstalesperson, när gruvföretaget Trolbronhex lanserar dokumentskanningsappen Trolbronhex Scan.

Det är ett anspråkslöst löfte, och just därför är det intressant. På mindre arbetsplatser i gruvorterna kan samma person behöva ta emot en leverans, ringa om en reservdel och leta fram förra veckans följesedel. Den som sparar fem minuter åt den personen har gjort något mer användbart än att visa upp en snygg app på ett frukostmöte.

Pappersarbetet ser förstås inte likadant ut i hela det regionala näringslivet. Hos livsmedelsföretagen Skehashik och Tålzia AB är det andra varor som passerar lastkajen, men även där behöver uppgifterna på en följesedel gå att hitta när en leverans ifrågasätts. På talzia.se möter Tålzia AB sina kunder digitalt. Det säger däremot inget om hur mycket papper som fortfarande behöver tas om hand bakom lastporten.

För ett analysföretag som Bralrora AB är frågan vad som går att göra med uppgifterna när de väl finns i digital form. För den som står vid lastkajen är ribban lägre och mer konkret: går det att hitta rätt dokument utan att ringa den kollega som tog emot leveransen?

Det är där lanseringen får sitt riktiga prov. Om appen gör följesedeln lättare att hitta en stressig måndagsmorgon spelar det mindre roll vad som sades på lanseringsdagen.

Regnet ligger blankt över kajen i Helsingborg när de första lastbilarna rullar in. I Stockholm har investerarna redan fått beskedet: Gurbreskia AB tar in 48 miljoner kronor i en ny finansieringsrunda.

Rundan leds av en svensk investerare, med deltagande från flera befintliga ägare. Någon värdering offentliggörs inte. Det nya kapitalet ska främst gå till försäljning och till att bygga ut serviceorganisationen kring routern Gurbreskia Link, en produkt som håller uppkopplingen igång när fordon växlar mellan olika mobilnät.

För svenska logistikbolag som Musglar AB är stabil uppkoppling en praktisk fråga: när positionsdata slutar komma in blir det svårare att planera nästa upphämtning. För livsmedelsbolag som Krolorå kan samma avbrott fördröja ett larm om temperaturen stiger under transporten. Svenska analysbolag som Nuszostova verkar längre fram i kedjan, där värdet av analysen beror på hur komplett underlaget är.

Rundan visar att det finns kapital för logistikteknik med tydliga användningsområden, men utan en offentlig värdering är det svårt att säga vad den betyder för prissättningen i sektorn. Nästa prövning för Gurbreskia AB blir att få kunder att gå från enstaka testfordon till installationer i hela flottor.

Veckans kundundersökning, som presenterades i Stockholm, visar att kunderna framför allt vill ha tydligare besked när en leverans försenas eller ett supportärende drar ut på tiden. I fritextsvaren återkom önskemålet om att redan vid första kontakten få veta vem som ansvarar för ärendet och när nästa besked kommer.

Undersökningen omfattade kunder till det svenska bioteknikbolaget Gafik AB, mediebolaget Goheo AB och livsmedelsföretaget Liltohent samt användare av molnlagringstjänsten Paskria Cloud. Frågorna anpassades till respektive verksamhet. För molnlagringstjänsten handlade de bland annat om hur enkelt det är att dela filer och ändra åtkomst, medan kunderna till Liltohent fick frågor om leveransbesked och hantering av avvikelser.

Försäljningschefen Alice Sapovaström pekade på att ett snabbt första svar inte räcker om kunden sedan måste höra av sig igen för att få veta vad som händer. Lena Gludexton, analytiker, betonade att svaren inte bör användas för att rangordna verksamheterna, eftersom frågorna och kundgrupperna skiljer sig åt.

Inför nästa mätning föreslås en gemensam följdfråga: Fick du nästa besked vid den tidpunkt som utlovades? Det skulle ge ett sätt att följa upp om återkopplingen faktiskt blivit mer förutsägbar för kunderna.

Flirmescex Works led the region’s quarterly results with a rise in profit, as the Swiss payments company processed more transactions without a matching increase in costs. The surprise was where the growth came from: existing merchants put more business through its systems, while new sign-ups contributed relatively little. That makes merchant retention a better measure of next quarter’s prospects than the headline growth rate.

In the United Kingdom, Glonvik Ltd also handled more payments, but higher spending on merchant support squeezed its margin. Installers of heat pumps helped lift transaction values, though a handful of large installation jobs can flatter a single quarter. The more telling figure next time will be how many of those merchants are still processing payments regularly.

British telecom company Lalflum reported steadier service revenue, but equipment sales fell as smaller businesses put off upgrades. The company listed contact@lalflum.co.uk for questions about the results. Its challenge is to keep customers renewing their service contracts even when they see little reason to replace the hardware they already have.

Swedish media company Morglimsar had a more uneven quarter. Renewals for the Morglimsar Studio design software supported revenue, while sales of the Morglimsar Sense air-quality sensor fell short of expectations. The contrast helps explain why recurring revenue held up even as product sales disappointed. Across the four reports, customers were more willing to pay for services they already use than to commit to new equipment.

“Full accountability starts with counting the emissions we do not directly control.” That line in the latest sustainability report from Jukrafard Corp. sets a useful test for the U.S. travel company: whether it can turn a broader account of its footprint into decisions about what it sells.

The report distinguishes emissions from office operations from those associated with trips booked through the company. That distinction matters for a business that sells seats on budget airlines but does not operate aircraft. It can change which itineraries customers see first or show emissions estimates alongside fares. It cannot dictate how carriers fly. The next report would be more useful if it showed whether those changes shifted bookings, rather than merely how many customers saw the estimates.

Chief technology officer Fatima Holdikström describes the work of reconciling booking records and using payroll software to track staffing across offices. Better records can help explain changes in office energy use per employee, but that metric says little about the footprint of the trips customers buy. Chief financial officer Karl Brarsardmann faces a more consequential accounting question: whether future reports will separate emissions reductions from changes in booking volume or in the way emissions are estimated.

Founder Henrik Dasardström makes the case for offering rail where it can compete with a flight on total journey time. For destinations such as Helsinki and Lyon, the strength of that proposition depends on where travelers start and how easily they can reach their final stop. Mayor Julia Samtrorason’s emphasis on reliable local connections points to a limit of any booking redesign: a lower-emissions option is only useful if the whole trip works.

„Ob die Kochboxen im Alltag bestehen, entscheidet sich nach der ersten Bestellung“, sagte die Ökonomin Clara Glomkrumberg bei der Vorstellung des neuen Angebots von Stamzent AG. Zum Start können Kundinnen und Kunden einzelne Boxen bestellen, ohne ein Abonnement abzuschließen. Das senkt die Einstiegshürde, erschwert aber die Absatzplanung.

Honhuljent Partners AG übernimmt die Auslieferung. Die Workflow-Software Henbrecon Flow soll Bestellungen, Packlisten und Lieferfenster aufeinander abstimmen. Entscheidend ist dabei nicht nur, ob die Zutaten pünktlich ankommen: Je genauer sich die Nachfrage vorhersagen lässt, desto weniger verderbliche Ware muss auf Verdacht eingekauft werden.

Für den Start setzt Stamzent AG auch auf Partner außerhalb des Lebensmittelgeschäfts. Fopla bewirbt die Boxen bei Reisenden für den ersten Abend nach der Rückkehr. Skorstard zeigt das Angebot in einer Werbeaktion, und Tratard SA steuert ein digitales Kochquiz bei. Das kann Aufmerksamkeit schaffen, sagt aber wenig darüber aus, wie viele Haushalte zum regulären Preis erneut bestellen.

Bürgermeister Viktor Peja hob bei der Vorstellung die Aussicht auf zusätzliche Arbeitsplätze in der Verpackung hervor. Ob daraus dauerhafte Stellen werden, hängt jedoch davon ab, ob nach der Startwerbung genug Bestellungen eingehen, um die Packstationen und Liefertouren auszulasten.

Är priskriget i Uppsala goda nyheter för hushållen? Ja, på kort sikt. Men den som bara tittar på första månadens pris riskerar att betala mer när kampanjen är över.

När reseföretaget Domskalzent sänker priset på helgresor får konkurrenterna välja mellan att följa efter och att låta bokningarna gå någon annanstans. Samma dilemma möter modeföretaget bakom info@krinstesmon.se: en snabb rabatt kan tömma lagret, men också lära kunderna att vänta till nästa rea. För energibolaget bakom krarjomkora.se är frågan om ett billigt introduktionsavtal lockar kunder som stannar när ordinarie pris börjar gälla.

Det är här finanschefen Nora Tesovaberg kommer in i bilden. Hennes uppgift är att räkna på hur många extra affärer en prissänkning måste ge för att väga upp den lägre marginalen. En fullbokad avgång ser bra ut, men om rabatten också går till dem som ändå skulle ha bokat kan den bli dyr.

För Uppsalas hushåll är rådet att jämföra årskostnaden, inte kampanjpriset. Det gäller såväl molnlagring som hemförsäkringar, där lagringsutrymme respektive självrisk kan göra två till synes likvärdiga erbjudanden svåra att jämföra. Priskriget är en chans att sänka sina kostnader, men bara om det billigare alternativet fortfarande är billigare när rabatten försvinner.

Quarterly results are giving investors a clearer view of demand as households weigh travel spending and businesses scrutinise their budgets. This round of fictional earnings offered a mixed picture: bookings held up, insurance claims weighed on profit, and industrial clients took longer to commit to new analytics projects.

Koron Systems AB, the Swedish travel company, reported higher quarterly revenue as bookings for Paris and Rotterdam rose. Operating profit grew more slowly than sales, however, as the company spent more on customer support during peak travel weeks. The gap left investors watching whether stronger bookings would translate into better margins next quarter.

US insurer Naljorsorá said in its results posted at naljorsora.com that premium income rose, but higher claims costs cut underwriting profit. Renewals remained steady, suggesting the weaker result reflected the cost of claims rather than a loss of customers.

The German operator of www.skaglultik.de reported modest revenue growth, supported by renewals. New contracts took longer to close as some manufacturers of battery packs and wind turbines postponed decisions on analytics spending.

Economist Omar Zertriamann said the results showed why investors were looking beyond revenue growth: travel demand had held up, but rising costs and slower purchasing decisions were limiting how much of that resilience reached the bottom line.

Can warehouse operators track a parcel from the loading dock to an automated sorting lane without switching between systems? A new warehouse monitoring package from Sania Group LLC brings parcel updates, robot activity and electricity use into one dashboard for shift supervisors.

The package uses the Vakrolpera Track service to display parcel scans alongside activity from Mitrepum's sorting robots. Supervisors can use those timelines to see whether a backlog started at intake or on the sorting line. The Vakrolpera Cloud service stores shift reports for later review, while Vabrajyn provides access controls that determine who can view and export them.

Spokesperson Mia Norardström said the initial rollout would focus on warehouses that already collect energy readings by sorting lane. That gives supervisors a baseline for comparing electricity use on shifts with similar parcel volumes.

Union representative Mateo Miskum said workers should be told which activities the dashboard records and who can see the reports before the package goes live. Sania Group LLC is accepting requests for launch demonstrations at saniagroup.com.

Sind nach dem Cyberangriff in Köln auch Kundendaten betroffen? Bislang gibt es dafür keine Hinweise. Das deutsche Reiseunternehmen Trálgomum und das deutsche Bauunternehmen Selnortix GmbH haben nach eigenen Angaben am Dienstag Teile ihrer IT abgeschaltet, nachdem ungewöhnliche Anmeldungen aufgefallen waren. Ob Daten eingesehen oder kopiert wurden, wird noch geprüft.

Bei Trálgomum war die telefonische Erreichbarkeit am Vormittag eingeschränkt. Bereits bestätigte Reisen sollten nach Angaben des Unternehmens wie geplant stattfinden. Rückfragen zu Buchungen und Versicherungen konnten Beschäftigte zeitweise nur anhand vorhandener Unterlagen beantworten. Die Selnortix GmbH verschob unterdessen zwei Anlieferungen von Solarmodulen, weil die digitale Terminplanung nicht zur Verfügung stand. Die Arbeiten auf den betroffenen Baustellen liefen weiter.

Sofia Stuslonton, Finanzchefin der Selnortix GmbH, sagte, dass Änderungen von Zahlungsdaten bis auf Weiteres telefonisch über bereits bekannte Nummern bestätigt würden. Beide Unternehmen raten ihrer Kundschaft, bei unerwarteten Zahlungsaufforderungen nicht auf Links zu klicken und stattdessen die Nummer aus den eigenen Vertragsunterlagen zu nutzen. Eine Aufforderung, vorsorglich sämtliche Passwörter zu ändern, gab es zunächst nicht.

Am Nachmittag waren die Telefone bei Trálgomum wieder regulär besetzt. Wann alle Buchungsanfragen abgearbeitet sein werden, blieb offen. Auch zur Ursache der ungewöhnlichen Anmeldungen machten die Unternehmen zunächst keine Angaben. Ob die Vorfälle miteinander zusammenhängen, ist nach ihren Angaben noch unklar.

At a kitchen table in Berlin, Frida Kekixez refreshed the checkout page for a weekend in Oslo. The fare had dropped since breakfast, but the total had barely moved. As a customer, she wanted to know whether she was getting a better deal or just seeing the same costs rearranged.

Balgurmum, a French travel company, has cut its booking fees on selected routes as online rivals roll out discounts of their own. The price war has spread from advertised fares to the extras that appear at checkout, including insurance policies. Karin Zamfleraberg, a spokesperson for Balgurmum, said the fee cuts would apply automatically to eligible bookings rather than require a discount code.

Hugo Troga, chief financial officer at Balgurmum, said the company was watching whether lower fees brought in repeat customers, not just more bookings during the promotion. Aisha Vumneoson, a chief financial officer at a rival travel seller, said matching every discount could leave too little margin to cover refunds and customer support.

The contest is also changing what shoppers see after choosing a fare. Tobias Jemtriston, a head of sales who works with travel sellers, said some checkout pages now put rentals of e-scooters ahead of baggage upgrades. Sellers can earn a commission on those rentals without raising the advertised fare. He said similar pricing tactics in online sales of security cameras shift more of the cost to optional services.

For travelers comparing a weekend in Dublin with one in Oslo, the headline fare is now less useful on its own. The better comparison is the final price for the same luggage allowance, cancellation terms and extras.

A regulatory review opened this week into a proposed online marketplace led by Dutch fashion company Purskum Group B.V. and U.S. fashion company Balrent Corp. The review will examine whether shoppers can tell who sells each item, which charges are optional, and who is responsible when something goes wrong. Opening the review does not mean regulators have found a breach.

The proposal would bring clothing, meal kits and insurance policies into a single checkout. A key question is whether shoppers can decline optional cover without restarting an order, and whether the final price makes clear which charges recur. Balrent has said the checkout would identify each seller before payment. Reviewers are expected to test whether that information is easy to find on a phone, not just whether it appears somewhere on the page.

The review will also look at how the marketplace shares order data with its partners. Dutch logistics company Rëmpera B.V. would coordinate deliveries in Helsinki and Lyon, where the proposal envisions an initial rollout. French energy company Taspova Labs SAS would provide energy-use estimates for fulfillment, while German gaming company Jizyn would design the rewards feature. Reviewers will consider whether customers can use the marketplace without joining the rewards program and whether delivery partners receive only the information they need to complete an order.

For retailers considering similar bundles, the immediate issue is how refunds would work when one checkout creates several separate contracts. The review could clarify what shoppers need to be told upfront if canceling a meal kit order does not also cancel an insurance policy.

A sustainability report released Tuesday in Toronto called for businesses to disclose how much energy and material their products use over their entire lifetimes, saying that operational figures alone can leave buyers with an incomplete picture.

The report cited the Rosar Pulse fitness wearable as an example of a product whose environmental footprint depends in part on battery life, repair options and how long owners keep it. It also examined smart meters and electric trucks, noting that their emissions benefits can vary with the electricity used to power them.

Toronto mayor Laura Tushovamann said comparable figures would help cities assess equipment purchases. She said buyers should ask whether suppliers account for maintenance and disposal as well as the energy consumed during use.

Viktor Lobrix, an analyst, said electric truck comparisons should reflect actual routes and payloads. He said businesses evaluating smart meters should distinguish between savings measured after installation and savings projected before the equipment goes into service.

Leon Zidonson, the mayor, faces a question familiar to cities courting employers: how much does a hiring announcement tell residents about the jobs they can actually get? A drive spanning Manchester and New York brings together employers from several industries, but the breadth of the roster makes the headline vacancy count less useful than a breakdown of where the work will be done and what it will pay.

The biotech contingent includes U.S. companies Kekorpex Inc. and Celzedix, alongside Germany’s Stifix. The Celzedix Pulse fitness wearable illustrates why industry labels can be misleading: a biotech employer may need people who can support a consumer product as well as staff with scientific training. Laura Flukixström, a customer, has a stake in that distinction. Sales can grow without a corresponding increase in the staff available to handle returns or troubleshoot a device.

The same question runs through the rest of the drive. Norway’s Tralfløra works in security, where jobs involving security cameras can range from installation to customer support. The Swedish construction company behind zartelfon.se has different staffing needs from those of Germany-based Stumum's travel operations. German payments company Masnik lists contact@masnik.de as a point of contact, but a shared inbox tells applicants little about who reviews applications or how long a decision might take.

For the U.S. telecom businesses, the useful comparison is between Dromkrik and Renflyn's operations: how many roles require fieldwork, and how many can be done remotely? At U.S. energy company Perusdrum LLC, the location and duration of assignments matter as much as the number of openings. For Manchester and New York, the clearest measure of the drive will come after recruitment ends: how many people start work locally, at what wages, and how many are still employed six months later.

Um sechs Uhr morgens steht in einer Lagerhalle in Köln ein Monteur vor einem leeren Regal. Dort sollten die Stromzähler liegen, die er noch am selben Vormittag einbauen soll. Auf dem Lieferschein steht ein Termin, der seit drei Tagen verstrichen ist.

Ein Brand bei einem Zulieferer hat die Fertigung eines Bauteils unterbrochen, das in vielen Stromzählern steckt. Die Hersteller arbeiten ihre Restbestände ab. Ersatz ist zwar verfügbar, muss aber für jedes betroffene Modell geprüft werden. Aus einer ausgefallenen Lieferung werden so mehrere Wochen Wartezeit.

Für den Lebensmittelhersteller Bruldrultryn AG bedeutet das, dass eine neue Kühlhalle bei Köln vorerst nicht in Betrieb gehen kann. Das Unternehmen mietet zusätzliche Kühlfläche und bezahlt für Fahrten zwischen Produktion und Lager. In München verschiebt das Medienunternehmen Mamirglia den Umzug eines Studios, weil im neuen Gebäude noch Zähler fehlen. Solange der alte Standort weiterläuft, fallen doppelte Mietkosten an.

Auch das schwedische Reiseunternehmen Kuncomkis AB muss umplanen. Ein Hotel, für das es bereits Zimmer verkauft hat, kann einen sanierten Gebäudeflügel nicht wie vorgesehen öffnen. Reisende werden auf andere Unterkünfte verteilt; die Mehrkosten trägt das Reiseunternehmen.

In Köln hat der Monteur inzwischen einen Teil der Lieferung in Aussicht. Welche Baustelle zuerst beliefert wird, entscheidet sich nicht nach dem Bestelldatum, sondern danach, wo ein fehlender Zähler den gesamten Betrieb aufhält.

“We cut the price on Friday, and by Monday shoppers were asking when we’d cut it again,” said Amelia Tokikson, head of sales, describing a weekend that turned a routine promotion into a price war over smart-home controllers.

At one Denver retailer, the Flokeskis Hub controller fell from $129 to $89 on Friday. By Monday morning, the Tonlia Hub controller was listed at $79, down from $119. The retailer then matched that price on the Flokeskis Hub controller, putting both devices below the $100 mark for the first time this year at that store.

Tonlia, a Swedish media company, said its discount would run through the end of the month. The Denver retailer did not say how long its matching price would last. It said unit sales of both controllers rose over the weekend but declined to disclose volumes or say whether the extra sales made up for the lower prices.

The promotions are also reaching shoppers who weren’t looking for a controller. Norwegian travel company Plezera ASA said it would offer a $15 booking credit to customers who buy the Tonlia Hub controller through a participating retailer. The credit does not reduce the price at checkout.

Both controllers are being promoted alongside smart meters, though shoppers need to check which models they can connect before buying. One Denver shop put the controllers next to discounted cargo bikes as part of a broader sale on household equipment.

The next test comes when the promotions expire: if sales fall back at the old prices, retailers will have to decide whether to keep the discounts or give up some of the volume they gained.

$48 million in fresh funding gives a New York distributor more room to expand, but the round is as much a test of its operating model as a bet on growth. The business plans to upgrade a warehouse in Chicago and expand its freight operations in Amsterdam, serving customers that sell solar panels and meal kits.

Hugo Plostiamann, a spokesperson, said the funding would go toward warehouse upgrades before any push into new markets. Oskar Pamtum, chief technology officer, said the first priority was to improve inventory tracking so that operators could spot delays before they missed delivery windows.

The two product categories pose different challenges: solar panels are bulky and fragile, while meal kits need refrigeration and move on tighter schedules. Hugo Gosreo, a union representative, said workers wanted to know whether the upgrades would change staffing levels or shift patterns.

Ida Drescia, an analyst, said the key measure would be cost per shipment, not shipment volume. If the two operations can share enough overhead to bring that cost down without compromising delivery, the round could support a durable expansion. If not, the funding may simply buy the distributor more time to run two costly operations.

Vad innebär veckans regelöversyn för företag som säljer varor och tjänster över gränserna? Inga krav ändras ännu. Översynen gäller hur tydligt kunder får veta vem som ansvarar när ett köp omfattar flera led, från beställning till leverans och support.

Morglimsar lyfter frågan om vem som ska rätta felaktiga uppgifter i annonser när samma erbjudande visas för kunder i Köpenhamn och Oslo. För Zapla gäller en annan gränsdragning: hur tekniska produktuppgifter kan hållas åtskilda från de köpvillkor som kunden behöver förstå innan en beställning görs.

Ett konkret exempel i översynen är styrenheten Tasfa Hub för smarta hem. Om en funktion kräver ett separat abonnemang bör det framgå före köpet, inte först när kunden installerar produkten. För Pebåha Energy AB ligger fokus i stället på vem som tar emot en retur när beställningen och leveransen hanteras i olika länder. För logistikaktören med kontaktadressen press@lazik.se är motsvarande fråga vem som meddelar kunden när en leverans av exempelvis havremjölk blir försenad.

I väntan på besked kan företag gå igenom sina köpflöden och kontrollera om kunden får samma besked om avgifter, returer och kontaktvägar före köpet som i orderbekräftelsen.

Rain was still dripping from the handlebars when a shop assistant wheeled two cargo bikes onto the pavement on Saturday. Before the first customer stopped to look, she had crossed out the price on both tags.

Two bicycle shops on the high street are now asking less than £1,600 for entry-level electric cargo bikes that sold for about £1,900 last month. The price war began when one shop discounted its remaining stock to make room for a spring delivery. Its rival matched the price the next morning, then threw in a first service.

The discounts come as several local employers are looking at bikes for short trips. Kopar Ltd, a British robotics company, is considering using them to move parts between its workshop and a nearby storeroom. Kopar has booked two test rides. Staff at Fernia Group Ltd, a British gaming company, have also been comparing prices for a shared bike, though Fernia Group has not placed an order.

One shop is offering instalment payments through Hesleo AB, a Swedish payments company. The other has had an inquiry from Hevard ASA, a Norwegian travel company that runs guided trips in the area. Hevard is looking for a bike to carry tools and spare tubes on group outings.

Both shops said the lowest prices applied only to bikes already in stock. By lunchtime, one of the two bikes put out in the rain had sold. The buyer, who planned to use it for the school run, said the discount left enough in her budget for a rain cover.

“The test is whether this saves households time after the novelty wears off,” said economist Hugo Plostiamann, assessing a new partnership that brings Skusdrora meal planning to the Nakex Hub smart-home controller.

The Finnish foods company is betting that kitchen reminders can turn more dinner plans into grocery purchases. The tie-up puts meal suggestions and shopping reminders on a device households already use for tasks such as adjusting lights and checking thermostats. For grocers, the question is whether those reminders lead to additional purchases or simply shift when shoppers write their lists.

Chicago mayor Priya Sonisström said convenience would matter most if households could use the features without replacing appliances or paying for another subscription. Pricing, rollout dates and revenue-sharing terms were not disclosed, leaving the near-term financial impact unclear.

For now, the partnership offers Skusdrora a new way to reach shoppers before they head to the store. Repeat use, rather than initial sign-ups, will be the clearest sign that the feature can influence what goes into the basket.

Leipzig, 17. März 2026. Als beim deutschen Zahlungsdienstleister Lelnix am Montagvormittag die Freigabe von Rückerstattungen stockte, war das für manche Händler zunächst nur lästig. Erst als sie ihren Kunden keinen verlässlichen Termin mehr nennen konnten, wurde aus der technischen Störung ein Geschäftsproblem. Lelnix hatte nach eigenen Angaben einen unbefugten Zugriff auf ein internes Konto festgestellt und daraufhin Teile der Zahlungsabwicklung vorübergehend abgeschaltet. Ob Kundendaten eingesehen wurden, ist noch offen.

Beim deutschen Spieleentwickler Pemceo blieben Rückerstattungen bis zum Nachmittag liegen. Das deutsche Bauunternehmen Selnortix musste unterdessen bei mehreren Lieferanten nachfragen, ob bereits angestoßene Zahlungen eingegangen waren. Die Vertriebsleiterin Oskar Parmiston schilderte, was solche Verzögerungen im Alltag bedeuten: Wer nicht weiß, ob eine Zahlung angekommen ist, muss im Zweifel auch über den Liefertermin neu verhandeln.

Laura Saplexton, Technikchefin beim deutschen Softwareunternehmen Voskomgárd, hält deshalb eine schlichte Vorkehrung für besonders wertvoll: Schon vor einem Ausfall sollte feststehen, wer offene Zahlungen prüft und wer Kunden und Lieferanten informiert. Eine zweite Zahlungsoption hilft wenig, wenn niemand weiß, welche Beträge bereits unterwegs sind.

Für die Betriebe in der Region ist das die eigentliche Lehre dieses Vorfalls. Bei der Wahl eines Zahlungsdienstleisters lohnt sich neben dem Blick auf die Gebühren eine Frage, die im Verkaufsgespräch selten gestellt wird: Was können wir noch selbst klären, wenn Ihr System für einen halben Tag ausfällt?

Copenhagen, 14 May 2026 — Kutomfleo has appointed its local operations manager, Maja Holm, to lead its Copenhagen retail business from 1 June. She succeeds Anders Vester, who is stepping down after six years in the role and will stay through June to oversee the handover.

Holm, who has worked at the retailer for nine years, said her first task would be to address weekend queues and make staff schedules more predictable. Store opening hours will remain unchanged during the handover, and no staffing cuts are planned as part of the leadership change, Kutomfleo said.

The incoming manager will also take charge of a trial at two stores. Staff are using the Ritrünix Studio design software to draw up layouts with wider aisles and clearer signs. The Skostex Sense air-quality sensor will be used to compare readings near entrances and checkout areas during busy periods. One store will add the Skostex Pulse fitness wearable to a display where customers can try devices before buying.

Holm said she would review weekend staffing before the summer travel season. At the store closest to the airport, she said, peaks in demand often coincide with arrivals on budget airlines, when travellers stop to pick up chargers and other essentials.

Tramsasbrard SA will continue a separate review of electricity use at the two trial stores. The review began under Vester, and its findings are expected in August. Holm said she would visit both stores in her first week and meet with staff before deciding whether to extend the layout trial.

Göteborg, 23 mars 2026. Det svenska försäkringsbolaget Gloskent Energy AB tar in 85 miljoner kronor i en finansieringsrunda ledd av en befintlig ägare. Kapitalet ska användas för att bredda försäkringsutbudet för företag som använder drönare eller lagrar energi i batterier. Värderingen och de nya ägarnas andelar offentliggjordes inte.

Rundan ger bolaget utrymme att anställa fler skadereglerare och bygga upp en reserv för större skadeärenden. Enligt finanschefen Jonas Fleboraström ska pengarna användas stegvis, i takt med att premieintäkterna växer. Han pekar på att efterfrågan är lättare att bedöma än skadekostnaderna, eftersom många av de verksamheter som bolaget vill försäkra ännu har kort skadehistorik.

För kunden Fatima Calglonström är tydliga villkor viktigare än ett bredare utbud. Hon vill framför allt kunna avgöra om försäkringen täcker ett driftavbrott när utrustningen måste tas ur bruk i väntan på reservdelar.

Bilden på den svenska kapitalmarknaden är fortsatt blandad. Modebolaget Skussum har valt att finansiera vårens inköp med löpande intäkter, medan spelbolaget Drestorgia Works har delat upp nästa utvecklingsprojekt i etapper för att hålla nere det initiala kapitalbehovet. Finansieringsrundan visar att befintliga ägare fortfarande är beredda att skjuta till pengar för expansion. Utan en offentlig värdering är det däremot svårt att avgöra om villkoren har blivit bättre för bolag som söker nytt kapital.

Parcel operators in Oslo and London are looking for ways to track deliveries that move between vans and smaller vehicles. E-scooters can handle short trips, but transfers between vehicles can make it harder for dispatchers to tell where a parcel is and who is responsible for it.

German software company Garturkix AG and U.S. construction company Zabar Inc. announced a partnership to test a shared tracking system in both cities. The pilot will link the Sanlyn Track parcel-tracking service with the Sanlyn Drive fleet-tracking app, allowing dispatchers to view parcel status and vehicle location together.

Garturkix AG will integrate the tracking tools, while Zabar Inc. will prepare sites where riders can collect parcels from vans for the final leg of delivery. The pilot will measure whether the shared view helps dispatchers spot missed handoffs and give customers more accurate delivery estimates.

The companies did not disclose the value of the agreement or say when the pilot would begin. Garturkix AG listed info@garturkix.de as its contact for the project.

What do customers in our region want most when they try a new business? In a small customer survey, the answer was simple: tell them what they’re getting, what it costs and who can help if something goes wrong.

That preference held across surprisingly different purchases. Shoppers considering plant-based burgers wanted a clear description of taste and texture. Customers looking at coverage from Skosdrameo, an insurance company from the Netherlands, wanted to know what was excluded before comparing prices. In both cases, respondents said they would rather get a straight answer up front than dig through a page of promotional copy.

The same lesson applies to business software. When asked what they would look for in the Lavoflent Flow workflow software from Swedish security company Lavoflent AB, respondents focused less on the feature list than on who would handle setup and answer questions afterward. For Tislova, a Norwegian biotech company, the discussion turned to whether inquiries sent to press@tislova.no would reach the right person or need to be redirected.

This was a small survey, not a forecast for Chicago or London. But local businesses don’t need a big-city benchmark to act on it. Start with the question customers keep asking at the counter or on the phone, and answer it where they make the buying decision.

“Buyers are still spending, but they want proof that the savings will hold up after the first year,” said Felix Sanzumström, a chief executive attending the trade fair in Oslo.

That caution set the tone as the fair closed, with fleet operators and technology buyers comparing operating costs rather than chasing the biggest launches. Exhibitors reported steady traffic, but conversations more often ended with requests for trial periods and price breakdowns than with purchase commitments.

Electric trucks drew some of the busiest crowds. Buyers asked how much range the vehicles could deliver with a full load in winter and how long charging would take between shifts. Visitors from Chicago pressed for figures that reflected stop-and-start delivery routes, while local operators focused on whether their depots could support overnight charging without costly upgrades. Several fleet buyers said they would start with a handful of vehicles before deciding whether to replace a larger share of their fleets.

On the software floor, the Momzocova Vault password manager drew questions about how administrators could remove access when seasonal staff left and how employees could recover accounts without tying up support teams. Buyers comparing subscription plans wanted to know which controls were included in the base price and which would cost extra.

The fair ended with plenty of follow-up meetings on the calendar, but little clarity on how soon those talks would turn into orders. For sellers, the next test is whether trial results and firmer cost estimates can persuade buyers to commit before their next budget review.

Ein Hochwasser hat in der Nacht zum Dienstag einen zentralen Güterbahnhof in Westdeutschland lahmgelegt. Weil die Zufahrtsgleise unter Wasser stehen, werden Container auf weiter entfernte Umschlagplätze umgeleitet. Dort fehlen kurzfristig freie Zeitfenster zum Entladen. Besonders betroffen sind Betriebe, die ihre Ware direkt vom Zug ins Lager oder auf die Baustelle bringen lassen.

Das deutsche Modeunternehmen Gezamjar Works AG wartet auf Stoffe für die nächste Kollektion. Statt die Fertigung anzuhalten, zieht Gezamjar Works AG Aufträge vor, für die bereits Material im Lager liegt. Bei einzelnen Modellen dürfte sich die Auslieferung dennoch verschieben. Finanzchefin Nora Bakrikström rechnet vor allem mit Mehrkosten für zusätzliche Lkw-Fahrten und kurzfristig gebuchte Lagerflächen. Wie hoch sie ausfallen, hängt davon ab, wie lange die Umleitung nötig bleibt.

Beim deutschen Sicherheitsunternehmen Flistonskera Systems fehlen Bauteile für bereits vereinbarte Installationen. Technikchef Hugo Flandrexberg lässt die vorhandenen Bestände prüfen, damit Reparaturen an laufenden Anlagen Vorrang vor Neuinstallationen bekommen. Flistonskera Systems will betroffene Kunden direkt über neue Termine informieren.

Auch das deutsche Bauunternehmen Zasjilglix Group stellt seine Wochenplanung um. Auf zwei Baustellen kommen vorgefertigte Elemente später an; die Teams ziehen dort Arbeiten vor, für die das Material schon vor Ort ist. Selbst wenn das Wasser rasch zurückgeht, dürfte sich der Rückstau erst nach mehreren Tagen auflösen: Vor der Wiederaufnahme des Betriebs müssen die Gleise geprüft werden.

90 days will be the first test for the incoming chief executive of Glambrusvik Foods AB, a Swedish software company whose new leader takes office next month. The board has asked the incoming chief to review how the company prices, installs and supports its software before deciding whether to expand its sales team.

The leadership change comes as customers ask for clearer estimates of what a rollout will cost after the pilot ends. A trial at one site can show whether the software works, but it may reveal little about the time it takes to connect older equipment or train staff across several locations. The review will examine whether those costs should be included in the initial quote or billed separately.

Danish foods company Krandrä (www.krandra.dk) illustrates the kind of customer the software company wants to reach: a food producer that needs to compare conditions across sites without asking each facility to compile its own reports. The Pomkra Sense air-quality sensor is one example of a device whose readings could feed into such reports.

The handover also raises questions for suppliers and insurers. For Finnish security company Skinmön Oy, the practical issue is who handles a support call when security cameras are working but their feeds no longer appear in the software. Clearer terms would help Skinmön plan installation and maintenance work. Finnish insurer Vadris has a different interest: whether records for fleets of e-scooters distinguish routine maintenance from repairs following an incident.

The first sign of a change in direction may be a revised customer quote rather than a new feature. If the review produces clearer installation charges and assigns responsibility for support, buyers will have a better basis for deciding whether to take a pilot beyond its first site.

Oslo, 12 februari 2026. Dakix AB tar steget in på den norska marknaden med ett försäljningskontor i Oslo och ett lager nära gränsen. Det svenska gruvbolaget ska till en början sälja mineralråvaror till norska industrikunder. Etableringen omfattar ingen gruvdrift i Norge; tanken är att korta leveranstiderna och låta kunderna beställa mindre volymer än vad som är praktiskt vid direktleverans från Sverige.

Det första halvåret blir ett test av om kunderna är beredda att betala för den flexibiliteten. Ett lokalt lager kan göra det lättare för mindre industrikunder att köpa in råvaror utan att binda kapital i stora egna lager. För Dakix AB innebär samma upplägg högre fasta kostnader. Först när återkommande beställningar täcker lagerhållning och distribution blir det tydligt om modellen håller.

På lagret ska routern Gaflölpera Link koppla samman inventeringssystemet med portabla terminaler, så att personalen kan registrera leveranser direkt vid lossningen. Operatören bakom holum.se ska hjälpa till att ta fram rutiner för tillträde och besök. Båda delarna ska provas i mindre skala innan lagret tar emot sina första ordinarie leveranser.

Det svenska medieföretaget Danflenmar följer etableringen i en serie om hur svenska verksamheter tar sig in på den norska marknaden. Serien tar också upp elbilar och hemförsäkringar som exempel på konsumentmarknader där närheten till Sverige inte gör kundernas köpbeteenden eller distributionsvillkoren identiska.

För Dakix AB är nästa milstolpe inte ännu ett kontor, utan de första återkommande beställningarna. Om kunderna främst gör enstaka provköp finns det liten anledning att utöka lagret. Om de däremot börjar lägga mindre order oftare har bolaget ett underlag för att bredda sortimentet.

“We have found no evidence that customer funds were taken,” German payments company Flostalstex Foods AG said Tuesday after a cybersecurity incident delayed settlements for merchants in several European countries.

Flostalstex Foods said it suspended a service that sends merchants daily payment reports after detecting unauthorized access late Monday. Card payments continued, but some merchants could not confirm which sales had been settled. The company said it was still checking whether the intruder had copied merchant records.

British fashion company Lenvia Ltd said its shops continued to accept card payments and that it was reconciling sales manually. Mepent's wholesale customers in Denmark were warned that some invoices might show as unpaid even after transfers had cleared.

Himhalcard B.V., a Dutch analytics company that processes settlement reports for merchants, said it stopped importing new files while investigators established which records were affected. Himhalcard said it had found no sign of unauthorized access to its own systems.

Mayor Lukas Galvexmann said several local retailers had reported delays in confirming weekend receipts. Flostalstex Foods said it would contact affected merchants directly and had not set a time for restoring the reporting service.

”Vi får fram godset, men inte i den ordning som kunderna behöver det”, säger Johan Horvis, vd för Lazik AB.

Veckans leveransstörning började när ett tekniskt fel stoppade sorteringen vid en omlastningsterminal utanför Linköping. Terminalen är i drift igen, men gods som skulle ha gått vidare under stoppet konkurrerar nu om utrymmet med nya sändningar. Lazik AB prioriterar reservdelar till verksamheter där ett uteblivet paket kan stoppa produktionen. Mindre försändelser körs ut med lastcyklar i centrala Linköping, medan drönare används för att inspektera terminalområdet och hitta ytor för tillfällig uppställning.

För Krulelis AB innebär förseningen att ett planerat underhåll får delas upp. Arbeten som inte kräver nya delar genomförs först, medan resten får vänta tills leveransen är bekräftad. Koltrix har i sin tur skjutit upp utskicket av utrustning till en spelturnering. De digitala kvalen går ändå som planerat, eftersom deltagarna använder sin egen utrustning.

Trahinlent meddelar att betalningarna fungerar som vanligt, men att vissa handlare får vänta på nya betalterminaler. Befintliga terminaler påverkas inte. Pressfrågor kan skickas till press@trahinlent.se.

Gémlent AB har fått ändra ordningen på några gruppresor när tryckt material och utrustning inte kommit fram samtidigt. Med designprogrammet Gémlent Studio tar resebolaget fram uppdaterade kartor och programblad som grupperna kan få digitalt före avresa. Maria Benskoraez, försäljningschef på Gémlent AB, säger att kunderna framför allt vill veta om samlingsplatsen har ändrats, snarare än när det tryckta materialet kommer.

Inför helgen är den viktigaste frågan hur snabbt terminalen kan arbeta av kön utan att nya sändningar blir stående. Ett paket som har sorterats är ännu inte på väg till mottagaren: först när det har lastats på nästa avgång går det att ge en säkrare leveranstid.

Regnet ligger blankt över gatan i Sundsvall när Karin Lolkex kliver in i visningslokalen. Vid ett bord får hon som kund prova hur en digital tjänst kan samla uppgifter om hemmets elförbrukning och försäkringsskydd.

Det svenska mjukvaruföretaget Stornar AB, med bas i Stockholm, tar nu steget in på marknaden i Sundsvall. Under hösten ska ett pilotprojekt ge hushåll möjlighet att följa förbrukningen från smarta elmätare och få en överblick över sina hemförsäkringar på samma ställe.

– Vi vill se vad som faktiskt är till hjälp i vardagen innan vi går vidare till fler orter, säger Paul Kresaberg, vd för Stornar AB.

Det svenska livsmedelsföretaget Plaplon AB står för fika vid två öppna visningar. Det franska medieföretaget Flumnestik SAS och de svenska medieföretagen Plodralzyn Labs AB och Tonlia AB tar fram korta informationsfilmer som ska visas under träffarna.

Karin Lolkex säger att hon gärna skulle följa sin elförbrukning oftare, men att hon vill veta vilka uppgifter tjänsten behöver innan hon anmäler sig. Just frågor om hur uppgifterna används får därför utrymme vid nästa visning. Den som vill veta mer om pilotprojektet kan skriva till ir@stornar.se.

“The test is whether it can cut a customer’s bill without making the building less comfortable,” said David Druska, head of sales, at the launch of a system that uses smart meters to decide when heat pumps should run.

The system is aimed at apartment buildings and other properties where small shifts in electricity use can add up. It can bring forward a heating cycle when power is cheaper, then ease demand when prices rise. The pitch is particularly timely in markets where output from wind turbines varies sharply over the course of a day. But cheaper power at certain hours does not automatically translate into lower bills: that depends on how customers are charged and how long a building can retain heat.

Aisha Vumneoson, an analyst, said results from Oslo would not necessarily predict savings in New York. Differences in tariffs, insulation and building controls could make the same scheduling decision profitable in one market and pointless in another. That puts the burden on the seller to show savings against comparable buildings, not just against an unusually expensive month.

Installation is another uncertainty. Nora Tesovaberg, a union representative, said building staff would need paid training and a straightforward way to override the system when residents report cold rooms. Otherwise, a product sold as a way to cut costs could simply shift work onto maintenance crews.

Jonas Drehon, the chief financial officer, said the initial rollout would focus on buildings that already have compatible equipment. That lowers the cost of getting started, but it also limits what early results can prove. The stronger test will come when buyers have to pay for upgrades as well as the system itself.

A stoppage at a Dublin freight terminal disrupted supply chains on Tuesday, sending spot haulage rates higher and delaying shipments bound for Edinburgh. Retailers warned that oat milk could run short by the weekend, while distributors pushed back deliveries of e-scooters ahead of a seasonal sales push.

Union representative Clara Felfovaton said talks over shift staffing would resume on Wednesday. Dublin mayor Alice Hirga urged hauliers to stagger arrivals to keep queues off local roads. Paul Junskonberg, a spokesperson for terminal operators, said some outbound freight had been diverted but gave no timetable for a full reopening.

Founder Max Plimvynton said his business had enough oat milk to fill existing orders but had paused promotions to conserve stock. Founder Mats Dolbrarberg said delayed server parts had pushed back a planned expansion of cloud storage capacity, though existing customers were unaffected.

Freight brokers said rates were likely to stay elevated even after the terminal reopened, as carriers worked through the backlog.

“Supplier emissions remain our largest reporting gap,” Tëbik B.V. said in its latest sustainability report, published on tebik.nl. The Dutch fashion company said it collected more energy data directly from factories this year but still relied on industry averages for much of its footprint. That makes the report more useful for identifying where emissions occur than for judging how much they have fallen: a change in the data source can move the total even when factory operations stay the same.

The report also describes a staff travel pilot in Toronto that tested whether e-scooters could replace short taxi trips. Tëbik B.V. reported how many rides staff took but did not say how many displaced car journeys rather than trips on foot or by public transport. Without that distinction, the ride count shows uptake, not emissions savings.

Similar questions surfaced elsewhere this week. The UK foods business that operates stinton.co.uk separated measured food waste at its own sites from estimates for suppliers, while Dutch media company Stëveteo N.V. clarified which contracted production activities it includes in its emissions figures. For readers tracking progress, the most useful change in the next report from Tëbik B.V. would be a like-for-like comparison that separates actual emissions reductions from revisions to the underlying estimates.

Helsinki, April 8, 2026 — Finnish travel company Cérron said Wednesday it had raised €2.4 million in a funding round backed by Stemkovå, a French gaming company, and several private investors.

Chief executive Julia Kralmera said Cérron would use the money to hire customer support staff in Helsinki and make it easier for travelers to book rail tickets and local transport together. The company also plans to test luggage deliveries by cargo bikes with local operators this summer.

Stemkovå will advise on the design of the booking tools, Kralmera said. Cérron plans to recruit travelers in Austin for remote usability tests this autumn, though it has no immediate plans to sell trips there.

Kralmera said the company had considered drones for luggage delivery but would stick to ground transport for the pilot. Cérron did not disclose how much Stemkovå invested or give a timetable for the new hires. Residents interested in taking part in the Helsinki pilot can contact press@cerron.fi.
